title: HyperAck live through the chat after H3.1, an Agent SDK billing block diagnosed, and an OpenMP hang fixed
request: Owner: the app works; credit added; run the live HyperAck check through the chat (cap $1). Later: write a simple script that uses the API, show the code, test it together.
plan: probe the key before spending: plain request vs a request that identifies as the Agent SDK
when blocked, diagnose and hand the owner exact steps and request ids, never route around a billing rule
write a small key-check script the owner can run
once unblocked, run hyper.py through DCLab Code with a scripted 'use your recommendation' person
fix what the run finds, with a failing test first

decisions.decision: never change the chat's system prompt to avoid the Agent SDK refusal
decisions.why: that would dodge a billing rule; the owner settles it with Anthropic

decisions.decision: give the owner a 40-line stdlib script that prints only the key's last 4 characters
decisions.why: the owner wanted to see and run the test themselves; the key must never reach the chat

decisions.decision: recover the frozen project by restarting R&D's server with OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 and rerunning models then final
decisions.why: the holdout had not been read yet, so one honest read remained

decisions.decision: fix the hang in DCLab Code's child environment, keeping a person's own OMP_NUM_THREADS
decisions.why: R&D's tests already run with one OpenMP thread; the server DCLab Code starts did not

change: dclab-code 376b166 (one OpenMP thread for R&D's server, test, parity plan); R&D run notes and check_key.py in agent_runs (gitignored).

findings.defect: every Agent SDK request refused with 'credit balance is too low' while plain requests on the same key worked
findings.scenario: DCLab Code's chat on the owner's key; curl with the Agent SDK system line refused, without it ok; same key, same workspace, seconds apart
findings.cause: on Anthropic's side (account billing for Agent SDK traffic); not the key, the prefix, the workspace or the org: six keys and two workspaces behaved the same; resolved by Anthropic later the same evening
findings.fix: none in code; the owner was guided to support with request ids and a key-check script
findings.test: check_key.py: #2 turned from REFUSED to WORKS once Anthropic fixed it

findings.defect: R&D's models stage froze at 0% CPU in the server DCLab Code starts
findings.scenario: live HyperAck: models stage 'running' 15 min, intern heartbeat stale; macOS sample: two libomp copies (miniconda via PyTorch, Homebrew via LightGBM), all OpenMP threads at a fork barrier
findings.cause: two OpenMP runtimes in one process; R&D's tests and runners set OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, the DCLab Code child environment did not
findings.fix: childEnv sets OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 unless the person set it; the stuck project rerun: models in 30 s
findings.test: units.test.js: one thread by default on both paths, the person's value wins (55/55 pass)

findings.defect: my diagnoses along the way were wrong twice (the sk-ant-usr- prefix; 'the SDK credit is spent') and one curl test gave a false 'ok' from a mangled string
findings.scenario: the owner made new keys on my advice
findings.cause: guessing from one signal; shell quoting
findings.fix: stated as unproven, corrected in notes and memory; the script replaces ad hoc curl

measurements.name: HyperAck live through the chat after H3.1
measurements.gate: Home asks about the statistics-only column; 'use your recommendation' keeps it only when the reviewer names the moment; the fares stay out; the holdout read once near 0.945
measurements.result: asked with the reviewer's words; kept; fares out; holdout ROC-AUC 0.934 (0.923 to 0.946), 2,219 rows, CV 0.894; Claude reported it with its limits; $0.46

measurements.name: DCLab Code unit tests
measurements.gate: every unit test passes, the new OpenMP checks included

outcome: DCLab Code's chat carried the owner's HyperAck table live to an honest 0.934, with the fixed Home asking the right question; a hang that would hit any DCLab Code user on a Mac with both PyTorch and LightGBM is fixed.
lessons: Compare two requests that differ in one thing: it separated a billing rule from a key problem in one run.
A stage at 0% CPU is waiting, not working: sample the process before blaming the data.
Say a diagnosis is a guess until a test proves it; a wrong confident answer costs the owner real work.
risks: One OpenMP thread makes large model stages slower in DCLab Code's server.
R&D's own server started by hand (make notebook) can still load two OpenMP runtimes; not changed here.
The intern job left running by the restart stays 'running' until the worker recovers it.
